method: every FEN and both continuations replayed with python-chess; material recomputed from the full board after the whole shown line (en passant and promotions counted); checkmate, stalemate and legal-move counts read from the board; Stockfish depth 16 on the position before the move, after the played move and after the suggested move. The v2 answer key, detector code and implementation files were not opened.

systemic_findings.finding: in 146 of 201 cases what_happened and stronger_idea use the identical frame 'The shown line after <move> ...', so neither sentence says which move was actually played. The packet's own required check asks the visible wording to distinguish played history from counterfactual play; here only the field label carries that distinction.
systemic_findings.why_it_matters: a card that renders the sentence without its label -- a notification, an email line, a summary row -- becomes genuinely ambiguous, and v1 did not have this problem because it said 'You played X and ...' in the past tense
systemic_findings.suggested_fix: restore an explicit agent and tense on the played branch, e.g. 'You played X; the line then ...'

systemic_findings.finding: 8 rows repeat a claim already made about the same position and move: 1 pair inside 'Count the whole capture sequence' is byte-identical in every visible field and differs only in a hidden defensive continuation, and 7 more repeat the same sentence under a second family label
systemic_findings.why_it_matters: they inflate the review denominator and the per-family claim counts the promotion gate uses
systemic_findings.suggested_fix: deduplicate on (fen, played_move, visible_claim) before counting a family toward the gate
